gaps.sentence: Smoking can ___ serious harm to your health.
gaps.explanation: do harm to something is the fixed phrase; 'make harm' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: The children ___ great fun at the fair.
We ___ our shopping at the local market every Saturday.
gaps.explanation: do the shopping is the collocation for buying food and household goods.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.

gaps.sentence: I was slightly ___ by his rude reply.
gaps.explanation: slightly annoyed is a standard collocation; the other options are too strong to be 'slight'.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ your seats; the performance is about to begin.
gaps.explanation: take your seats is the formal way of asking people to sit down.

gaps.sentence: The critics ___ praise on the young violinist.
gaps.explanation: 'Heap praise on' = give a great deal of praise.

gaps.sentence: She ___ attention to every detail of the contract.
